title: Bric & Clé
description: Run a 1950s toy workshop: clients order strange objects made of lacquered pieces, brass diamonds and bars, and you build them with four moulds, a dial-driven Swapper, keys and wind-up tin automatons. Under the toy, every object is a logic formula and every gesture a proof step, checked by an independent verifier. Twelve orders and two open challenges. English by default, French available.
controls: Mouse or touch: drag an object by its base onto the Swapper, a dial, a cradle or a lock; click a piece to fill the armed dial; click an arrow to flip or unbox it.
Keyboard: Tab between objects, Enter to pick; E Swapper, K key, D Duplicator, N box, L flip arrow; Space pulls the lever; Ctrl+Z undo; Escape drops; H shows Hortense's notes; M mutes.
Settings: language, day or evening theme, colour-blind mode, animation speed and interface size.
credits: Cédric Bernadac — game design, after his course “Logique — livre I” (version 10).
Developed with AI assistance (Claude). Objects drawn by code.
